evals.prompt: I have a COCO detection dataset. Show me how to pass it to create_engine with getitune 0.4.0.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the COCO root markers, points data at the dataset root, and uses a compatible detection model.

evals.prompt: I want to train an Ultralytics YOLO model from a data.yaml file. How do I install and pass the dataset?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains installation of getitune 0.4.0 with the ultralytics and chosen hardware extras and the matching PyTorch index. It shows a clearly marked data.yaml placeholder passed through data or --data_root, without claiming installation or training was performed.

evals.prompt: Give commands and Python code only; do not install or train anything. On Linux with Python 3.12 and CPU, I need getitune 0.4.0 with Ultralytics YOLO support. My dataset is described by ./dataset/data.yaml and I will supply the model name in model_name. Show installation and how to pass this dataset to the engine, without cloning Geti.
evals.expected_output: Installs the pinned cpu and ultralytics extras with the CPU PyTorch index and passes the data.yaml path to create_engine(model=model_name, data=...). Does not require a checkout, reformat the dataset unnecessarily, or claim a completed run.
assertions: The installation selects getitune 0.4.0 with both cpu and ultralytics extras.
The installation supplies https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu as an extra index.
The engine receives ./dataset/data.yaml as data and model_name as the model.
Does not require cloning Geti, running uv sync or just, or claim installation or training occurred.
